text:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: multiple model-load failures in us-west-2 (pool-a). Symptoms: OOM during deserialization, followed by CUDA resets and container restarts. Some customer tiers seeing 503s. Auto-detect flagged 12 failures in the last 5m. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-load|model-load>
lex (eng-oncall): Ack, I'm taking lead. Which model family and node ids?
maria (runtime): Seeing it on model: llama2-13b-q8 and a few xformers variants. Example log from warmup:```[2026-03-16T22:01:12Z] warmup: deserializing weights shard-3 -> alloc 5.2G
[2026-03-16T22:01:13Z] runtime: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at /opt/runtime/src/cuda_kernels.cu:204
[2026-03-16T22:01:13Z] container: killed by OOM```
sam (infra): Node list: ip-10-0-8-42, ip-10-0-8-47, ip-10-0-8-51 in pool-a. GPU drivers show repeated resets on 08-47. Kernel logs show NVDIMM paging spikes.
kyle (sre): Is this correlated with a recent kernel/driver rollout?
maria (runtime): Not that I can see—driver version stable. Compile cache timeouts also seen for some models: `compile_graph timeout after 120s` which prolongs warmup and increases peak mem.
lex (eng-oncall): Ok mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily remove pool-a from routing for hosted traffic. 2) Trigger a rolling drain of the 3 affected nodes. 3) Promote fallback model variants (q4_0 quantized) for critical routes. 4) Notify customers and open an incident page. Who can run the drain?
sam (infra): I'll start the drain and cordon the nodes: `kubectl drain ip-10-0-8-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then reboot node and collect dmesg. Kicking off now.
prod-ops: We'll prepare a customer-facing note: short impact summary + ETA for rollback.
maria (runtime): For immediate fewer OOMs, reduce per-load batch-parallelism to 1 on warmup operator and disable compile parallelism: config patch:`warmup.batch_parallelism=1
warmup.compile_parallelism=0` Applying to canary now.
lex (eng-oncall): Good. Also create a temporary routing rule to prefer smaller quantized variants: `POST /admin/routing` payload: `{route: "/v1/generate", prefer_variant: "llama2-13b-q4"}` (ops-approved).
sam (infra): Rebooted ip-10-0-8-47, dmesg attached: "GPU 0: reset due to illegal address" and some page allocation failures. Uploading node logs to /mnt/incident/7843219999/logs.tar.gz
kyle (sre): If paging is the culprit, we should increase node swap and limit concurrent warmups. But swap increases may hide root cause. Suggest limiting concurrent warmups to 2 across the cluster for now.
maria (runtime): Can we add a short circuit: if deserialization exceeds 90s, abort and fallback to lighter variant? I can push a hotfix to the control plane to abort and fallback.
lex (eng-oncall): Please do that, maria. Also open a ticket to investigate compile-cache slowness (ID INC-7843).
prod-ops: Customer note draft: "We're investigating an issue causing model load failures and transient 503s in us-west-2. We're routing traffic away from affected nodes and applying mitigations. We'll update in 30m." Approve? :eyes:
sam (infra): Drain complete for ip-10-0-8-47 and ip-10-0-8-51. ip-10-0-8-42 showing high mem pressure but still online; cordoning it.
maria (runtime): Hotfix deployed: abort-on-long-deser and automatic fallback to q4 variants. Telemetry shows warmup error rate dropping from 12/min -> 1/min.
lex (eng-oncall): Nice work. Keep monitoring for 30m, then we can slowly bring nodes back. Assigning follow-ups: sam investigate kernel paging cause; maria profile deserializers and compile cache; kyle run postmortem.
prod-ops: Notifying customers now. Draft posted to incident page.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-7843219999 (priority P1). On-call: lex.
kyle (sre): Quick note for postmortem: capture sequence: deserialization spike -> compile timeouts -> prolonged warmup -> GPU resets -> container OOMs -> customer impact.
lex (eng-oncall): Agreed. I'll keep this thread as the coordination channel. If anything changes escalate to execs. :thumbsup:
